operating_notes.text: Dabur International Limited decided to incorporate Trustline Brands Inc. in Delaware, USA with capital of USD 10,000.
Recommended final dividend of ₹5.50 per equity share (550%) for FY26.
Management noted ~10% input cost inflation due to Middle East conflict, countered by 4% price hikes.
Dabur International completed the incorporation of Pravaah Consumer Group Inc. in Delaware, USA.
HPC revenue was ₹1,385 Cr (55% of domestic sales, up 12.3% YoY), Healthcare was ₹623 Cr, and F&B was ₹528 Cr in Q1FY27.
International business revenue stood at ₹1,006 Cr (27% of consolidated sales, up 15.5% YoY in INR terms).
Received FSSAI prohibitory order on 3 August 2026 restricting '100%' claim on select food product labels (honey, ghee, coconut water); initiated transition to revised packaging.
US FDA warning letter issued for data integrity lapses at Silvassa plant affecting private label exports
NCLT New Delhi sanctioned amalgamation scheme of Sesa Care Private Limited with Dabur India (Appointed Date April 1, 2026).
Q2FY27 update reported double-digit consolidated revenue and PAT growth, high-teens growth in Hair Oils, Shampoos, and Foods, but margin drag from inflation in HPC and OTC.

timeline.summary: Dabur India convened NCLT-ordered shareholder and unsecured creditor meetings on May 2, 2026, regarding the amalgamation of Sesa Care Private Limited.
Dabur India Limited’s NCLT-convened shareholders meeting adjourned for 30 mins due to insufficient quorum on May 02, 2026, resuming at 11:35 AM with quorum met.
Dabur India announced plans through its step-down subsidiary to incorporate a new US entity, Trustline Brands Inc.
Q4FY26 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,038.02 Cr (+7.3% YoY), net profit to shareholders ₹368.6 Cr (+15.1% YoY).
Dabur India reported Q4FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹3,038 Cr, up 7.3% YoY, with PAT rising 15.1% to ₹369 Cr.
Dabur India announced board approval for director re-appointments and a tenure modification ahead of the 51st AGM.
Ashok Kumar Jain, Group Company Secretary and Chief Compliance Officer, shared the audio recording link for Dabur India Limited’s Q4 FY 2025-26 Investors’ Conference Call on May 07, 2026.
Dabur India hosted its Q4FY26 earnings call on May 7, 2026, guiding for high single to low double-digit revenue growth in FY27.
Dabur India announced that its step-down subsidiary Dabur International completed the incorporation of Pravaah Consumer Group Inc. in Delaware, USA.
Dabur clarified USFDA audit observations at its Silvassa plant, stating no impact on operations or financials.
Dabur India promoters submitted regulation 31(4) disclosures confirming zero share encumbrance for FY26.
Q1FY27 results (consolidated): revenue ₹3,764.39 Cr (+10.6% YoY), net profit ₹586.16 Cr (+15.3% YoY).
Q1FY27 investor presentation: consolidated revenue up 10.6% YoY to ₹3,764.4 Cr with 5% India volume growth.
Dabur clarified receipt of an FSSAI prohibitory order regarding '100%' packaging claims on select food products and initiated label transitions.
2026-08-06: Dabur receives US FDA warning letter for data integrity issues at Silvassa plant
Dabur India Limited’s 51st AGM on August 06, 2026, approved ₹5.50 dividend per share (₹1 face value) for FY2025-26, payable by September 04, 2026.
NCLT New Delhi sanctioned the Scheme of Amalgamation of Sesa Care Private Limited into Dabur India Limited with Appointed Date April 1, 2026.
Guided for double-digit consolidated revenue and PAT growth in Q2FY27, led by broad-based India FMCG and international demand.

watchlist.response: Mohit Malhotra stated Glucose bounced back after April, with mid-teens growth in May and high teens growth in June, attributing the pattern to seasonality and rural consumption for instant energy, and denied any structural issue.
watchlist.text: Abneesh Roy asked about Glucose business recovery post-April disruption and whether there is a structural issue due to health perceptions and competition from energy drinks.

watchlist.response: Ankush Jain outlined a three-pronged strategy: acquisition (including D2C via ₹500 Cr allocation), dividend (100% of India profits), and routine capex, emphasizing that India cash is not being expanded for international business.
watchlist.text: Prakash Kapadia inquired about capital allocation strategy for the ₹9,500 Cr cash and investments on the balance sheet, suggesting dividend payouts or strategic acquisitions.
Completion of statutory filings to make Scheme effective
